investment_token_configured.meaning: investmentShareToken has been configured so _configureVaultInvestmentSettings() is invoked in registerVault()

vault_registered.meaning: a vault was previously registered through the registerVault() flow

max_allowance_granted.meaning: the vaultAddress was configured with max allowance for investmentShareToken

unregister_executed.meaning: unregisterVault() flow is executed for the previously registered vault

allowance.meaning: investmentShareToken allowance remaining on the (old) vault

assumptions: unregisterVault() is executed on the vault previously registered via registerVault(), i.e. old_vault
the allowance symbol denotes the investmentShareToken allowance granted to old_vault; the lingering max approval is captured as allowance != 0
allowance is treated as per-vault for the old_vault account

unresolved.description: The numeric value of the max allowance is not defined; the max-allowance precondition is bound as a Boolean flag rather than a numeric bound.
Report does not identify any actor or caller of unregisterVault(); the property does not depend on caller identity.
The investmentShareToken allowance has no stated unit or decimals; the allowance integer is bound as dimensionless.
The ordering/time relation between registerVault() and unregisterVault() beyond the described flow sequence is not specified.

limitations: The lingering allowance persisting even after the vault update (i_allowance_after_update) is deferred as a secondary consequence of the same core lingering approval.
Whether the old vault is malicious or the lingering allowance is actually spent is out of core scope; no exploitation is asserted.
How unregisterVault() updates state, reverts, or replaces the vault is not specified and is not modeled.
Whether the allowance is per-vault or shared across vaults is not asserted; the model assumes per-vault.
